traits.label: Overview
traits.text: Plant pathogenic fungus that specifically infects bird cherry (Prunus padus) leaves, causing characteristic 'pocket galls'. These are pouch-like deformities that occur on the leaves and are the result of the fungus manipulating the plant tissue. Taphrina padi belongs to the Ascomycota division, and its primary mode of reproduction is through the production of ascospores. This fungus is mainly of interest for its effect on bird cherry trees and is not used for culinary or medicinal purposes.
